title: Virtualization Engineer
summary: A virtualization engineer builds and runs the clusters where a company's virtual servers live, mostly on VMware vSphere, Microsoft Hyper-V or Nutanix. You sit in the infrastructure or data-centre team, keep hosts patched and healthy, and work with storage, network and backup engineers.
dailyDuties: Build and patch ESXi or Hyper-V hosts and vCenter
Create, resize and migrate virtual machines on request
Troubleshoot slow or failed VMs, hosts and datastores
Check backups and run restore and failover tests
Automate reports and routine tasks with PowerCLI scripts
Plan capacity and raise changes for upgrades
Work tickets and join incident calls with the infra team

skills.expectation: Build, patch and run VMware vSphere or Hyper-V clusters, including HA, DRS and vMotion
Run and troubleshoot guest servers on Linux or Windows Server
Run and troubleshoot guest servers on Linux or Windows Server
Present and manage datastores from SAN or NAS storage
Set up virtual switches, VLANs and port groups and fix connectivity
Automate builds, reports and checks with PowerCLI or PowerShell
Back up and restore virtual machines with Veeam, Commvault or similar
Plan failover and disaster recovery for VMs, for example with SRM or Zerto
Handle incidents and changes through ITIL processes and tickets
Run Nutanix AHV/Prism or vSAN clusters
Move VMs to Azure, AWS or another hypervisor
Provision VMs and clusters with Terraform or Ansible
Watch cluster capacity and performance with monitoring tools
Run hybrid workloads on Azure or Azure VMware Solution

groups.label: A server operating system (Linux or Windows Server)

certifications.why: Useful where VMs move to or run alongside Azure
Proves Linux administration for guest servers
Networking base for virtual switching and VLANs
Covers Hyper-V and hybrid Windows Server work.
Backup of virtual machines is part of most virtualization roles.
VMware is still the main platform in Indian data centres, and this is Broadcom's current VCP.
